Paragraph: Summary of Passage: Therefore, dedicate all your actions to the Supreme, direct your thoughts toward inner spiritual reality, shed expectations of personal gain, free yourself from possessiveness and mental lethargy, and perform your duty.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Arjuna's hesitation, emotional distress, and reluctance to engage in his required duty on the battlefield.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna delivers a direct call to action: dedicate all work to God (mayi sarvani karmani sannyasya), focus on the spiritual self (adhyatma-cetasa), drop selfish desire (nirasih), abandon ownership (nirmama), and cast off mental lethargy or hesitation (vigata-jvara).
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna receives a comprehensive, practical strategy to overcome hesitation and act with focus.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Overcoming Mental Paralysis: Eliminating anxiety and hesitation to take required action
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Purposeful Execution: Directing mental focus toward duty rather than personal gain
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Freedom from Egoic Ownership: Releasing possessiveness over resources and outcomes

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Adhyatma-cetasa (With mind absorbed in spiritual consciousness)
Nirasir nirmamo bhutva yudhyasva vigata-jvarah (Fight free from selfish desire, possessiveness, and mental fever)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Krishna commands Arjuna to surrender all work to Him, anchor his mind in divine consciousness, discard selfish expectation and possessiveness, and engage in battle free from inner agitation.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Mental paralysis is cured by clear purpose and detachment. When you surrender excessive control, abandon self-centered demands, and clear away mental lethargy, you can execute necessary tasks with confidence and composure.
